programs.title: Voices That Echo: Worker Voice in Agent-Managed Systems
programs.grade_or_level: Adult continuing education / union delegate training
outcomes: Explain how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO routes work and makes decisions
Identify where human decision rights are reserved and why worker voice belongs there
Practice drafting and debating a proposal through the Proposal Forum process

sessions.activity: Read the EchoDawn charter; map which powers stay with people (final vote, treasury, amendments) and discuss where delegates fit.
Role-play the Task Router: delegates assign tasks to working groups and discuss fairness, transparency and workload distribution.
Use an evidence summary template to assess how automation affects members' roles; compare notes on agent-generated summaries.
Small groups draft a workplace proposal, debate it, and hold a mock human final vote following the DAO's reserved-powers rule.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised session feedback and mock proposal themes (no names, employers or identifying details) contribute to shared models of how worker groups engage with DAO governance.
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary with written informed consent; learners choose what feedback to share, can opt out of data contribution at any time, and no personal or workplace identifiers are collected.

programs.title: Echo Explorers: Sunrise Science and Shared Governance
outcomes: Describe the temperate eucalypt forest ecosystem of the Jamison Valley and the Three Sisters
Explain how sound echoes work and how echoes inspired this DAO's name and listening-based design
Simulate a decision cycle where agents inform and humans decide

sessions.activity: Investigate the Blue Mountains biome: eucalypt forests, valley mist and why sunrise creates echoes at Echo Point.
Read a kid-friendly charter and identify which decisions only people can make; create a classroom charter together.
Teams draft a class proposal (e.g., a playground improvement) with an 'agent assistant' fact sheet, then debate and vote as humans only.
Build a progress tracker poster showing measurable outcomes of the class proposal and reflect on what worked.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised class voting patterns and proposal drafts (no names, ages or school identifiers) help build shared examples of youth civic learning in DAO worlds.
programs.consent: Guardian/parent written consent is required for all data contribution; individually de-identified contributions only, parents may withdraw consent at any time, and no personal data is collected from students without it.

programs.title: Governing AI as a Public Good: An NGO Field Guide
programs.grade_or_level: Professional / NGO program staff and managers
outcomes: Analyse the AGI Future Foundation mission model of agent-managed, human-governed organisations
Design a contribution model with measurable outcomes for their own programs
Apply evidence-synthesis and proposal cycles to NGO decision-making

sessions.activity: Study the mission of governing AI as a public good; draft measurable outcomes for a hypothetical NGO charter.
Practise summarising evidence with the Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent roles; critique agent-generated briefs.
Draft a real program proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter method; peer review before a human-only decision step.
Map task routing and working groups across a multi-partner program, identifying coordination gaps.
Set up a progress-tracking dashboard tied to charter outcomes and agree review checkpoints.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised proposal templates, outcome indicators and lessons learned (no organisational names or beneficiary data) feed shared models of NGO governance practice.
programs.consent: Staff opt in via written consent; beneficiary data is never shared, contributions are aggregated and de-identified, and organisations can withdraw their material at any time.

programs.title: From Mission to Measurement: Nonprofit Governance in an Agent-Assisted DAO
outcomes: Distinguish agent operations from human-reserved governance decisions (votes, treasury, appointments)
Translate mission statements into measurable charter outcomes
Run a steward-led decision cycle using the five-zone structure

sessions.activity: Compare their own mission statement to the EchoDawn charter; identify reserved human powers and steward roles.
Review how agents monitor and summarise evidence for boards; discuss trust, verification and bias checks.
Board members debate an agent-drafted proposal, amend it, and cast the final human vote - agents never enact.
Assign stewards to coordinate working groups between decision cycles using the Task Router model.
Define 2-3 measurable outcomes and a public progress report cadence for their organisation.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised governance patterns - decision-cycle timings, amendment frequencies, outcome framings (no organisation or donor identifiers) - support shared research on nonprofit DAO adoption.
programs.consent: Leadership provides organisational consent in writing; individual contributions are optional and de-identified, sensitive board or donor information is excluded, and withdrawal is possible at any time.
